decision_rule: Supported iff direction as hypothesised AND Holm-adjusted p < .05 within H1-H7
note: Hypotheses are defined in src/config.py and written to this registry BEFORE any test is executed in the same run. They were written after the Phase-1 audit, in which item-level descriptive correlations had been shown; specification was theory-led but not blind to those descriptives.

hypotheses.text: Satisfaction/expectation fulfilment is negatively associated with switching intention.
hypotheses.literature: Bansal et al. 2005 (dissatisfaction as push); Hsieh et al. 2012

hypotheses.text: Alternative attractiveness is positively associated with switching intention.
hypotheses.literature: Bansal et al. 2005; Hsieh et al. 2012; Chang et al. 2023 (pull significant)

hypotheses.text: Perceived competitor product choice/variety is positively associated with switching intention.
Perceived competitor promotional attractiveness is positively associated with switching intention.
hypotheses.literature: Pull factors in platform switching (Chang et al. 2023; e-grocery PPM 2023)

hypotheses.text: Perceived switching effort is negatively associated with switching intention.
hypotheses.literature: Burnham et al. 2003; Bansal et al. 2005; Chang et al. 2023 (mooring significant)

hypotheses.text: Familiarity with Zepto is negatively associated with switching intention.
hypotheses.literature: Habit/familiarity as mooring (Bansal et al. 2005; Cui et al. 2026 on inertia)

hypotheses.text: Inertia (continued-use tendency) is negatively associated with switching intention.
Push, Pull and Mooring composites jointly explain variance in switching intention (multiple regression, model F-test).
Current users who report having shifted some purchases (Q19=Yes) have higher switching intention than those who have not.
Former users whose most important reason was area/coverage have higher willingness to return than former users whose most important reason was voluntary (platform-choice).
